Three things I know about my little brother: he is seven, he cannot whistle, and he believes I can fix anything.

The third one is my fault. Last year I repaired his remote-control truck with a paper clip and some solder, and since then every broken object in the house has arrived on my desk. A zipper. A snow globe. Once, memorably, a sandwich.

Most of them I can't fix. What I can do is take them apart in front of him and show him why. The snow globe leaked because the seal was a ring of glue about 1 mm thick; the zipper failed because a single tooth had bent. He doesn't always follow, but he always watches, and lately he's started guessing before I open anything up.

He guessed right about the zipper.

I don't think I'm teaching him engineering. I think I'm teaching him that "broken" is a question, not an answer—and I'm learning it at roughly the same speed he is.
